page.title: Settings
page.description: Configure the console's appearance, notifications and security.

unreachable.title: Couldn't read this appliance's configuration
unreachable.description: The appliance could not load its settings. The values below may be defaults or outdated. You cannot save changes until the settings load again.

toast.connectLive: Connect to a live appliance to use this.

appearance.title: Appearance
appearance.description: Tune the console to your taste. Theme applies instantly; the rest saves with the section.

language.label: Language
language.description: The display language for the console.

theme.label: Theme
theme.description: Dark by default — the appliance is happiest at night.

accent.label: Accent
accent.description: The highlight colour for selected states and focus.

density.label: Density
density.description: Compact tightens table rows and spacing.

reduceMotion.label: Reduce motion
reduceMotion.description: Minimize animations and transitions throughout the console.

autoCollapse.label: Auto-collapse sidebar
autoCollapse.description: Collapse the navigation rail to icons on narrower windows.

timeZone.label: Time zone
timeZone.description: Every time in the console is shown in your browser's time zone, with its offset (GMT+3); hover one to see it in UTC. A job's schedule is shown in the job's own time zone, with your time beside it when the two differ. The browser's zone is set by your operating system.

events.title: In-console notifications
events.description: Pop-ups in this browser while the console is open; kept in this browser only. E-mail is set above.

jobFailure.label: Job failure
jobFailure.blurb: A backup run fails or errors

access.title: Access & policy
access.description: Change the password for your account.

session.title: Sign-out after inactivity
session.description: How long the console stays signed in while you are away. A click, a key press, a scroll or a page change counts as activity; the console's own background refreshes and a moving pointer do not.
session.label: Sign out after
session.hint: Applies immediately to this session, and to future sign-ins on this browser. A minute before, the console asks whether you are still there.

applyFailed.title: Inactivity timeout not applied
applyFailed.description: Saved locally, but the appliance couldn't be reached — it'll apply next time you sign in.

session.limit: Whatever the activity, this session ends at {{time}}: the appliance's limit from sign-in.
session.noLimit: The appliance sets no limit from sign-in: an active session stays signed in.

certificate.title: HTTPS certificate
certificate.description: The certificate this console and the REST API are served with. Both are only reachable over HTTPS; plain HTTP requests are redirected.
certificate.loadFailed: Couldn't read the certificate from the appliance.
certificate.sourceGenerated: Generated by this appliance and renewed automatically before it expires. Browsers show an untrusted-certificate warning for it until you install one from a trusted certificate authority.
certificate.sourceInstalled: Installed by {{user}} on {{when}}. It is not renewed automatically — install a replacement before it expires.
certificate.sourceManual: Placed on the appliance by hand. It is not renewed automatically — install a replacement before it expires.

warning.expired: This certificate has expired. Browsers refuse it without an explicit override — install a new one.
warning.expiresSoon_one: This certificate expires in {{count}} day and is not renewed automatically.
warning.expiresSoon_other: This certificate expires in {{count}} days and is not renewed automatically.
warning.expiresSoonAutoRenew_one: This certificate expires in {{count}} day; the appliance renews it automatically.
warning.expiresSoonAutoRenew_other: This certificate expires in {{count}} days; the appliance renews it automatically.
warning.noNames: The certificate lists no host names or IP addresses (subject alternative names). Browsers ignore the common name, so they reject it for every address.
warning.namesNotCovered: None of this appliance's own names or addresses ({{names}}) are in the certificate. Browsers will warn unless the console is opened through a name the certificate lists.

toast.reloaded: New connections already use it. Reload this page to switch this browser over.
toast.nextStart: Saved. The appliance serves it from its next restart.

revertDialog.title: Revert to a self-signed certificate?
revertDialog.description: The installed certificate and its key are removed, and the appliance generates a new self-signed certificate and serves it right away. Browsers will show an untrusted-certificate warning again, and CLI clients that trusted the current key will need to trust the new one.

form.title: Install a certificate
form.intro: Use a certificate issued by your certificate authority, or your own self-signed one. The appliance checks the pair before replacing anything, so a mistake leaves the current certificate in place.
form.certificateHint: The server certificate first, then any intermediate certificates. A combined .pem file that also holds the key fills both fields.
form.privateKeyHint: RSA (2048 bits or more) or EC (P-256, P-384, P-521). Stored on the appliance, readable only by its service.
form.passphraseHint: Only for an encrypted key. Used once to read it and not stored.
form.fileTooLarge: {{name}} is too large to be a PEM certificate or key.
form.fileNotPem: {{name}} has no PEM certificate or private key in it. Convert DER or PKCS#12 (.pfx) files to PEM first.
form.privateKeyRequired: Paste or load the private key.
form.installFailed: The appliance couldn't install this certificate.
form.afterInstall: New connections get the certificate straight away. CLI clients that trusted the previous key will refuse to connect until they trust the new one.

operator.label: Operator
operator.blurb: Run jobs & restores; no policy changes

users.title: Users
users.description: People who can sign in to this appliance and what they may do.

removeUser.title: Remove {{name}}?
removeUser.description: They'll immediately lose access to this appliance. Their audit history is retained. This can't be undone.

tokens.title: API tokens
tokens.description: Credentials for the AltaStor API, CLI and integrations.

empty.title: No API tokens
empty.description: Create a token to authenticate the API, CLI or Terraform provider.

revokeToken.title: Revoke {{name}}?
revokeToken.description: Any client using this token will immediately lose access. This can't be undone.

keyEscrow.title: Encryption key escrow
keyEscrow.description: A copy of your backup encryption keys that survives this appliance.
keyEscrow.warning: Keys for encrypted backups live only in this appliance's catalog. Lose the catalog and those restore points can't be decrypted — even though the data is safe in the repository. Export regularly and keep the archive somewhere else.
keyEscrow.passwordHint: At least {{count}} characters. It's the only thing protecting the keys and credentials inside the archive.

toast.doneDescription: {{jobs}} jobs and {{backups}} backups, with their encryption keys. Store it off this appliance.
toast.failedDescription: The appliance didn't produce an archive. Try again in a moment.

appliance.title: Backup server
appliance.probeFailed: Couldn't read hardware details from the appliance. Fields it reports are shown as “—”.

createToken.copyDescription: This is the only time the full token is shown. Store it somewhere safe.
createToken.createDescription: Tokens authenticate the AltaStor API and CLI. Scope them to the minimum needed.
createToken.treatLikePassword: Treat it like a password. Anyone with this token can act as <0>{{scope}}</0> client.

inviteUser.title: Invite user
inviteUser.description: They'll receive an invitation to set a password and enrol MFA.
inviteUser.name: Full name

users.title: Users
users.description: Who can sign in, and the one role each of them holds.
users.lastAdminNote: Disabling a user or giving them a new password signs them out everywhere. Nobody can change their own role, nor give a role or change a user allowing more than their own role. The last enabled Administrator can't be demoted, disabled or deleted, so someone can always manage users.
users.ownRole: You can't change your own role: another user who may manage users has to.
users.roleBeyondYours: This role allows functions yours doesn't, so you can't give it.
users.userBeyondYours: {{name}}'s role allows functions yours doesn't, so you can't change or delete them.

form.title: Add user
form.description: The user signs in with this name and password, and can do what the role allows.
form.name: User name

edit.title: Edit {{name}}
edit.description: Change the name the user signs in with, and their password. The role, and whether they can sign in, are set in the list.
edit.renameHint: The user signs in with the new name and keeps their password.
edit.passwordHint: Leave empty to keep the current one. A new password needs at least {{count}} characters and signs the user out everywhere.
edit.ownPassword: Your own password is changed under Settings → Security, which asks for the current one.

deleteDialog.title: Delete {{name}}?
deleteDialog.description: The user is signed out everywhere and can no longer sign in. Their entries in the audit log stay.

roles.title: Roles & permissions
roles.description: The roles a user can hold, built-in and custom.
roles.matrixDescription: What each role allows, function by function. Anything a role doesn't allow is disabled.

reason.builtIn: Built-in roles can't be changed or deleted. Clone one to make your own.
reason.ownRole: This is your own role: another user who may manage roles has to change it.
reason.beyondYours: This role allows functions yours doesn't, so you can't change or delete it.
reason.beyondYoursClone: This role allows functions yours doesn't, so you can't clone it.

roles.builtInNote: Built-in roles can't be changed, renamed or deleted; clone one to make a custom role. Every role allows signing in and out and changing one's own password. A change to a custom role applies to its users on their next action, without signing in again.

editor.description: The role allows exactly the functions ticked here; everything else is disabled. You can only grant what your own role allows.
editor.name: Name
editor.nameRequired: Enter a name for the role.
editor.beyondYours: Your role doesn't allow this, so you can't grant it.
editor.usersHint_one: {{count}} user holds this role and gets the change on their next action.
editor.usersHint_other: {{count}} users hold this role and get the change on their next action.

deleteDialog.title: Delete {{name}}?
deleteDialog.description: Nobody can be given this role any more. Its entries in the audit log stay.
deleteDialog.inUse_one: {{name}} is held by {{names}}. Give them another role first, then delete it.
deleteDialog.inUse_other: {{name}} is held by {{count}} users: {{names}}. Give them another role first, then delete it.
deleteDialog.inUseNoNames_one: {{count}} user holds {{name}}. Give them another role first, then delete it.
deleteDialog.inUseNoNames_other: {{count}} users hold {{name}}. Give them another role first, then delete it.

email.title: E-mail notifications
email.description: The appliance e-mails the recipients below when a chosen event happens, through your SMTP server.
email.liveOnly: Connect to a live appliance to set up e-mail notifications.
email.loadFailed: Couldn't read the e-mail settings from the appliance.

server.title: SMTP server

securityHint.starttls: Connects unencrypted, then switches to TLS before signing in (usually port 587).
securityHint.ssl: TLS from the first byte (usually port 465).
securityHint.none: Nothing is encrypted, the password included. Only for a relay on a trusted network (usually port 25).

server.verifyTlsOn: The certificate must be trusted by the appliance and name this server.
server.verifyTlsOff: Any certificate is accepted, so a machine in between could read the mail and the sign-in.
server.timeoutHint: How long to wait for the server, 5–300.

auth.title: Authentication
auth.noneHint: For a relay that accepts mail from the appliance without signing in.
auth.unencryptedWarning: The connection is not encrypted, so the sign-in crosses the network in the clear. Choose STARTTLS or SSL/TLS.

grantHint.client_credentials: The application signs in on its own and sends as the mailbox (Microsoft 365).
grantHint.refresh_token: A user consented once; the appliance refreshes the access token as needed.

oauth.mailboxHint: The account the token sends as.
oauth.refreshTokenHint: From the consent flow; a token the provider replaces is stored automatically.
oauth.scopeHint: Leave empty for the provider's SMTP scope.

secret.stored: Stored on the appliance. Leave empty to keep it.

addresses.title: Sender and recipients
addresses.recipientsHint: Every notification goes to all of them. Press Enter to add an address.

events.title: Events that send e-mail
events.hint: Switch an event on to e-mail the recipients when it happens.
events.threshold: Send when a repository is filled to

descriptions.job.failed: A job's run finished and the backup of at least one VM failed. One notification per run, covering every VM.
descriptions.job.warning: A job's run finished, every VM was backed up, and at least one backup reported a warning.
descriptions.job.succeeded: A job's run finished and every VM was backed up without a warning.
descriptions.repository.low_space: After a backup, a local or SMB repository's disk is filled to the threshold or beyond. Sent again once it has dropped below and filled up again.
descriptions.system.clock_jump: The server's clock moved further forward than expected, so retention deletes nothing until an Administrator confirms the time.
descriptions.tls.certificate_expiring: An HTTPS certificate an administrator installed expires within 14 days, or has expired. Checked daily.

test.checkInbox: Check that it arrived; a spam filter can still hold it. Unsaved changes were used but not saved.

failure.smtp_connection_failed: Couldn't connect to the SMTP server
failure.smtp_auth_failed: The SMTP server refused the sign-in
failure.oauth_token_failed: Couldn't get an OAuth 2.0 access token
failure.smtp_sender_refused: The SMTP server refused the sender address
failure.smtp_recipients_refused: The SMTP server refused the recipients
failure.smtp_error: The SMTP server didn't accept the message
failure.other: The test e-mail was not sent

error.summary_one: {{count}} setting needs attention before this can be saved or tested.
error.summary_other: {{count}} settings need attention before this can be saved or tested.
error.host: Not a host name or IP address.
error.hostRequired: Enter the SMTP server's host name or IP address.
error.usernameRequired: Enter the user name the server signs in.
error.passwordRequired: Enter the password for that user.
error.mailboxRequired: Enter the mailbox the token sends as.
error.googleGrant: Google issues no client-credentials tokens for mail; use a refresh token.
error.tenant: Enter a tenant ID (a GUID) or a domain name.
error.senderRequired: Enter the address notifications are sent from.

script.title: Custom script
script.description: Run your own script when a chosen event happens, to reach a chat system, a ticket queue or anything else e-mail doesn't.
script.enable: Run the script on its events
script.warning: The script runs on the appliance as the backup service's account, so it can do whatever that account can: read the catalog and the stored credentials, and change or delete backups. Upload only code you have read and trust.
script.unavailable: Scripts are switched off on this appliance (ABR_NOTIFICATION_SCRIPTS=0). A stored script does not run.
script.loadFailed: Couldn't read the script settings from the appliance.
script.viewDescription: The script as it is stored and run. Reading it is recorded in the audit log.
script.uploadFailed: The appliance didn't take the script.
script.noInterpreter: {{name}} doesn't start with a #! line naming its interpreter, such as #!/bin/sh.

removeDialog.title: Remove this script?
removeDialog.description: {{name}} is deleted from the appliance and stops running. Its run history stays.

script.timeoutHint: A run that takes longer is stopped, with whatever it started. {{min}}–{{max}}.
script.eventsHint: Chosen apart from the events that send e-mail. The script runs even with e-mail switched off.
script.testPassed: The script finished without an error.

receives.title: What the script receives
receives.stdin: The event as JSON on standard input, and in the file named by ABR_EVENT_FILE: event, name, severity, subject, body, time, host, version and details, the facts of the event (the job, its VMs and their results, for one).
receives.variables: The main fields as environment variables. None of the server's own variables reach the script, and the PATH is a fixed system one.
receives.outcome: Exit code 0 counts as success. A run that fails is recorded and not repeated. Treat every value as data: a VM's name, for one, comes from outside the appliance.
